questions.question: What is a random variable?
choices: A symbol whose value must always be positive
A numerical value assigned to an outcome of a random process
A number that changes without any probability model
The most common outcome in every experiment

questions.question: Which is a discrete random variable?
choices: The number of heads in four coin tosses
The exact height of a randomly chosen tree
The exact time a runner takes to finish
The exact mass of a water sample

questions.question: What is expected value?
choices: The largest possible value
The value guaranteed on the next trial
The value with the highest probability only
The probability-weighted mean of possible values

questions.question: What must the probabilities in a discrete probability distribution sum to?
choices: The number of outcomes

questions.question: Which formula calculates expected value for discrete values x and probabilities P(x)?
choices: Add the values without using probabilities
Add the products xP(x) over all possible values
Multiply all probabilities together
Choose the greatest value of x

questions.question: A variable is 0 or 10, each with probability 1/2. What is its expected value?
A fair six-sided die has outcomes 1 through 6. What is the expected numerical result?
Why can expected value differ from every possible single-trial outcome?
choices: It must always be rounded to an outcome
It gives the next result with certainty
It describes a long-run average
It ignores probabilities

questions.question: A variable equals 2 with probability 0.7 and 8 with probability 0.3. What is its expected value?
A raffle ticket costs $2 and has probability 1/100 of winning $50, otherwise winning $0. What is the expected net gain per ticket?
Which distribution is valid?
What does an expected net gain of zero mean for a wager under its stated model?
choices: Every participant breaks even on every trial
Winning is impossible
Average gains and losses balance in the long run
The next result must be zero

questions.question: A variable takes values 1, 2, and 3 with probabilities 0.2, 0.5, and 0.3. What is its expected value?
Why should the ticket price be subtracted when finding expected net gain?
choices: Net gain accounts for the amount paid to participate
The price changes the probability of winning
The prize already equals the net gain
Subtracting makes every expected value positive

questions.question: Which statement about negative expected net gain is correct?
choices: Every player loses on every trial
Winning has probability zero
The payout must be negative
Repeated play produces an average loss under the model

questions.question: A machine produces 0, 1, or 2 defective parts per batch with probabilities 0.6, 0.3, and 0.1. What is the expected number of defects per batch?
A choice pays $8 with probability 1/4 and $0 otherwise, and costs $1. What is its expected net gain?
Two prize drawings have the same expected payout. What can still differ?
choices: The variability and chances of different payouts
Their probability totals, if both are valid
The arithmetic definition of expected value
The requirement that each payout be positive

questions.question: An insurer estimates a 0.02 chance of paying a $1000 claim on a policy. Ignoring other costs, what is the expected claim payout per policy?
A project has probability 0.8 of earning $100 and probability 0.2 of losing $50. What is its expected net result?
choices: $50 gain
$90 gain
$70 gain
$30 loss
